spec_features.spec_quote: `submit{status: done|give_up}` is deliberately included so the model has a *clean exit*
spec_features.evidence: Tool declared in tools.py:67-83 (submit with enum done|give_up). dispatch() handles it returning terminal=True (tools.py:130-134). harness honors it: `if result["terminal"]: tr.terminal_status=result.get('status'); tr.stop_reason='submit'; break` (harness.py:165-168). TERMINAL_TOOLS={'submit'} (tools.py:88). End-to-end enforced: dispatched AND honored as a stop.
spec_features.notes: Both done and give_up route through the same terminal break, so the model can disengage at will.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: submit lets the model declare done so we can distinguish graceful stop from spiral

spec_features.spec_quote: stop after 3 consecutive no-tool-call "thinking" turns; a wall-clock `episode_timeout_s`; and `max_output_tokens` per turn
spec_features.evidence: All three enforced: (1) 3 consecutive no-tool turns -> _last_k_are_noop(tr.turns,3) returns True and breaks the loop with stop_reason='max_turns' (harness.py:153-156, helper at 201-204). (2) episode_timeout_s checked at top of each iteration: `if time.time()-start > cfg.episode_timeout_s: tr.stop_reason='timeout'; break` (harness.py:133-135). (3) max_output_tokens passed into the API call kwargs every turn (model_client.py:111, set from config.py:46).
spec_features.notes: Compound claim; every sub-mechanism actually runs and changes execution.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: avoid an infinite no-op loop against a real API / hard wall-clock budget per episode (defensive against runaway loops) / cap per-turn so a degenerate model can't run up unbounded cost

spec_features.evidence: Loop bound: `for i in range(cfg.max_turns):` (harness.py:131) with a for/else `else: tr.stop_reason='max_turns'` (harness.py:169-170). Default max_turns=30 (config.py:65, default.yaml). Enforced loop ceiling.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: max_turns: 30  # enough failures to trigger the spiral

spec_features.spec_quote: `early_stop_on_spiral` can halt an episode once a *stronger* deterministic detector fires
spec_features.evidence: online_detector built only when enabled: `online_detector = metrics_mod.online_detector_factory(cfg.metrics) if cfg.harness.early_stop_on_spiral else None` (runner.py:115-116), passed into run_episode. Harness checks and breaks: `if (cfg.early_stop_on_spiral and online_detector is not None and tr.n_turns()>=cfg.early_stop_min_turns): if online_detector(tr): tr.stop_reason='early_stop_spiral'; break` (harness.py:172-178). The factory builds a STRONGER detector with composite_min_signals raised by +1 (>=3) (metrics.py:208-216).
spec_features.notes: Off by default (config.py:75) but fully wired and halts execution when enabled; the 'stronger detector' claim is real.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: stop early once a spiral is confidently detected online to save cost / avoid stopping too eagerly and biasing the measurement
